3716-mrs-general-talboys.title: Mrs General Talboys
3716-mrs-general-talboys.creator: Unknown
3716-mrs-general-talboys.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. looking woman of some thirty or thirty-three years of age, with soft, peach-like cheeks,--rather too like those of a cherub, with sparkling eyes which were hardly large enough, with good teeth, a white forehead, a dimpled chin and a full bust. Such, outwardly, was Mrs. The description of the inward woman is the purport to which these few pages will be devoted.

arxiv-2111-04375.title: Solving spin systems: the Babylonian way. Thanks: This work has been supported by a DFG research grant, contract number 2337/1-1. It is my pleasure to thank Stephan Gufler, Goetz Kersting, Markus Petermann, Adrien Schertzer, Marius A. Schmidt, and Giulia Sebastiani for the endless discussions on the
arxiv-2111-04375.creator: Nicola Kistler
arxiv-2111-04375.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Nicola Kistler. We show that spin systems with generic (ferro- or paramagnetic, or random) interactions are ”completely integrable”. The approach is worked out, by way of example, for the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model: we derive an exact formula for the quenched free energy in finite volume which involves an integral over a Gaussian field with correlation structure given by the interaction matrix (with a twist).

arxiv-2301-04279.title: Collective flows of protons and deuterons in Au + Au collisions at E b ​ e ​ a ​ m = 1.23 E_{beam}=1.23 A A GeV by the IQMD model
arxiv-2301-04279.creator: Ling-Meng Fang(房灵猛), Yu-Gang Ma(马余刚) ID, Song Zhang(张松) ID
arxiv-2301-04279.description: Abstract Collective flows of protons and deuterons for Au + Au collisions at beam energy E b ​ e ​ a ​ m E_{beam} = 1.23 A A GeV were simulated by an Isospin dependent Quantum Molecular Dynamics (IQMD) model. Two coalescence models, namely naive coalescence and dynamical coalescence models, for the formation of deuterons are compared.

arxiv-2304-01857.title: FAST: Fidelity-Adjustable Semantic Transmission over Heterogeneous Wireless Networks
arxiv-2304-01857.creator: Peichun Li 1 , 2 , Guoliang Cheng 1 , Jiawen Kang 1 , Rong Yu 1 , Liping Qian 3 , Yuan Wu 2 , and Dusit Niyato 4
arxiv-2304-01857.description: Abstract In this work, we investigate the challenging problem of on-demand semantic communication over heterogeneous wireless networks. We propose a fidelity-adjustable semantic transmission framework (FAST) that empowers wireless devices to send data efficiently under different application scenarios and resource conditions.

arxiv-2307-09739.title: Potential Tertiary Effects on the LISA Verification Binary HM Cancri
arxiv-2307-09739.creator: Naoki Seto
arxiv-2307-09739.description: Abstract Two groups recently analyzed the long-term orbital evolution of HM Cancri, which is one of the most important verification binaries for the space gravitational wave detector LISA. By using the reported first and second derivatives of its orbital frequency f f , we discuss potential tertiary effects on this binary.

arxiv-2312-03407.title: Extremal Fitting CQs do not Generalize
arxiv-2312-03407.creator: Balder ten Cate, Maurice Funk, Jean Christoph Jung, Carsten Lutz
arxiv-2312-03407.description: Abstract A fitting algorithm for conjunctive queries (CQs) produces, given a set of positively and negatively labeled data examples, a CQ that fits these examples. In general, there may be many non-equivalent fitting CQs and thus the algorithm has some freedom in producing its output.

arxiv-2406-01584.title: SpatialRGPT: Grounded Spatial Reasoning in Vision-Language Models
arxiv-2406-01584.creator: An-Chieh Cheng, Hongxu Yin, Yang Fu, Qiushan Guo, Ruihan Yang, Jan Kautz, Xiaolong Wang, Sifei Liu
arxiv-2406-01584.description: Abstract Vision Language Models (VLMs) have demonstrated remarkable performance in 2D vision and language tasks. However, their ability to reason about spatial arrangements remains limited. In this work, we introduce Spatial Region GPT (SpatialRGPT) to enhance VLMs’ spatial perception and reasoning capabilities.

arxiv-2409-04225.title: FPT Algorithms using Minimal Parameters for a Generalized Version of Maximin Shares
arxiv-2409-04225.creator: Klaus Jansen, Alexandra Lassota, Malte Tutas, Adrian Vetta
arxiv-2409-04225.description: Abstract We study the computational complexity of fairly allocating indivisible, mixed-manna items. For basic measures of fairness, this problem is hard in general. Thus, research has flourished concerning input classes where efficient algorithms exist, both for the purpose of establishing theoretical boundaries and for the purpose of designing practical algorithms for real-world instances.

arxiv-2409-09503.title: A class of exactly solvable Convection-Diffusion-Reaction equations in similarity form with intrinsic supersymmetry
arxiv-2409-09503.creator: Choon-Lin Ho
arxiv-2409-09503.description: Abstract In this work we would like to point out the possibility of generating a class of exactly solvable convection-diffusion-reaction equation in similarity form with intrinsic supersymmetry, i.e., the solution and the diffusion coefficient of the equation are supersymmetrically related through their similarity scaling forms. I Introduction Stochastic phenomena are rather ubiquitous in the world we live in.

arxiv-2501-10496.title: Extension of Symmetrized Neural Network Operators with Fractional and Mixed Activation Functions
arxiv-2501-10496.creator: Rômulo Damasclin Chaves dos Santos, Jorge Henrique de Oliveira Sales
arxiv-2501-10496.description: Abstract We propose a novel extension to symmetrized neural network operators by incorporating fractional and mixed activation functions. This study addresses the limitations of existing models in approximating higher-order smooth functions, particularly in complex and high-dimensional spaces. Our framework introduces a fractional exponent in the activation functions, allowing adaptive non-linear approximations with improved accuracy.

arxiv-2503-07511.title: PointVLA: Injecting the 3D World into Vision-Language-Action Models
arxiv-2503-07511.creator: Chengmeng Li, Yichen Zhu, Junjie Wen, Yan Peng, Yaxin Peng, Feifei Feng
arxiv-2503-07511.description: Abstract Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models excel at robotic tasks by leveraging large-scale 2D vision-language pretraining, but their reliance on RGB images limits spatial reasoning critical for real-world interaction. Retraining these models with 3D data is computationally prohibitive, while discarding existing 2D datasets wastes valuable resources.

arxiv-2508-10826.title: The Future is Fluid: Revolutionizing DOA Estimation with Sparse Fluid Antennas Thanks: ( Corresponding author: Tuo Wu. ) H. Xu is with the School of Cyber Science and Engineering, Ningbo University of Technology, Ningbo 315211, China (E-mail: xuhebest ​ @ ​ sina . com \rm xuhebest@sina.com ). T. Wu
arxiv-2508-10826.creator: He Xu, Tuo Wu, Ye Tian, Ming Jin, Wei Liu, Qinghua Guo, Maged Elkashlan
arxiv-2508-10826.description: Abstract This paper investigates a design framework for sparse fluid antenna systems (FAS) enabling high-performance direction-of-arrival (DOA) estimation, particularly in challenging millimeter-wave (mmWave) environments. By ingeniously harnessing the mobility of fluid antenna (FA) elements, the proposed architectures achieve an extended range of spatial degrees of freedom (DoF) compared to conventional fixed-position antenna (FPA) arrays.

arxiv-2509-25023.title: Generalization of Variadic Structures with Binders: A Tool for Structural Code Comparison
arxiv-2509-25023.creator: Alexander Baumgartner, Temur Kutsia
arxiv-2509-25023.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Alexander Baumgartner, Temur Kutsia. This paper introduces a novel anti-unification algorithm for the generalization of variadic structures with binders, designed as a flexible tool for structural code comparison. By combining nominal techniques for handling variable binding with support for variadic expressions (common in abstract syntax trees and programming languages), the approach addresses key challenges such as overemphasis on bound variable names and difficulty handling insertions or deletions in code fragments.

arxiv-2512-15491.title: GazeBlend: Exploring Paired Gaze-Based Input Techniques for Navigation and Selection Tasks on Mobile Devices
arxiv-2512-15491.creator: Omar Namnakani a,* , Yasmeen Abdrabou b , Jonathan Grizou a ,c , and Mohamed Khamis a
arxiv-2512-15491.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Omar Namnakani a,* , Yasmeen Abdrabou b , Jonathan Grizou a ,c , and Mohamed Khamis a. The potential of gaze for hands-free mobile interaction is increasingly evident. While each gaze input technique presents distinct advantages and limitations, a combination can amplify strengths and mitigate challenges.

pmc-10575313.title: Genetic Diversity Analysis of Soybean Collection Using Simple Sequence Repeat Markers
pmc-10575313.creator: Alibek Zatybekov, Moldir Yermagambetova, Yuliya Genievskaya, Svetlana Didorenko, Saule Abugalieva
pmc-10575313.description: Soybean [Glycine max (L.) Merr.] is a nutrient-rich crop that offers a sustainable source of dietary protein and edible oil. Determining the level of genetic diversity and relationships between various genetic resources involved in breeding programs is very important in crop improvement strategies.

pmc-10610537.title: Regulation of Tumor Apoptosis of Poriae cutis-Derived Lanostane Triterpenes by AKT/PI3K and MAPK Signaling Pathways In Vitro
pmc-10610537.creator: Shuai Yue, Xi Feng, Yousheng Cai, Salam A Ibrahim, Ying Liu, Wen Huang, Maria Dolores del Castillo, Rosaria Maddalena Ruggeri
pmc-10610537.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Poria cocos is traditionally used as both food and medicine. Triterpenoids in Poria cocos have a wide range of pharmacological activities, such as diuretic, sedative and tonic properties. In this study, the anti-tumor activities of poricoic acid A (PAA) and poricoic acid B (PAB), purified by high-speed counter-current chromatography, as well as their mechanisms and signaling pathways, were investigated using a HepG2 cell model.

pmc-10643977.title: Transcriptional profiles reveal histologic origin and prognosis across 33 The Cancer Genome Atlas tumor types
pmc-10643977.creator: Hui Xiao, Liang Hu, Qi Tan, Jinping Jia, Ping Xie, Junai Li, Minghua Wang
pmc-10643977.description: BackgroundIn recent years, with the development of transcriptome sequencing, the molecular characteristics of tumors are gradually revealed. Because of the complexity of tumor transcriptome, there is a need to look for the molecular signatures which can be used to evaluate the tissue origin and cell stemness of tumors in order to promote the diagnosis and treatment of tumors.

pmc-11344112.title: Rapid antigen detection of severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus-2 in stray cats: A cross-sectional study
pmc-11344112.creator: Ronaldy Santana Santos, Daniel Antônio Braga Lee, Marina dos Santos Barreto, Eloia Emanuelly Dias Silva, Pamela Chaves de Jesus, Pedro Henrique Macedo Moura, Deise Maria Rego Rodrigues Silva, Jessiane Bispo de Souza, Taynar Lima Bezerra, Patricia Oliveira Meira Santos, Adriana Gibara Guimarães, Luca
pmc-11344112.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Background and Aim:Although reverse zoonotic transmission events from humans to domestic cats have been described, there is currently little evidence of severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus-2 (SARS-CoV-2) circulation in stray cats. Due to the evidence of natural and experimental infections in cats and the capacity to disseminate the virus among them, this study aimed to identify the SARS-CoV-2 antigen in stray cats from the Federal University of Sergipe in Brazil.Materials and Methods:One hundred twenty six stray cats from the university were screened

pmc-11492378.title: Harvest Initiated Volatile Organic Compound Emissions from In-Field Tall Wheatgrass
pmc-11492378.creator: Gregory
pmc-11492378.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). While crop and grassland usage continues to increase, the full diversity of plant-specific volatile organic compounds (VOCs) emitted from these ecosystems, including their implications for atmospheric chemistry and carbon cycling, remains poorly understood. It is particularly important to investigate VOCs in the context of potential biofuels: aside from the implications of large-scale land use, harvest may shift both the flux and speciation of emitted VOCs.

pmc-11510043.title: Differential Regulation of L-Arginine Metabolism through NOS2 and Arginases during Infection with Trypanosoma cruzi
pmc-11510043.creator: Arturo A Wilkins-Rodríguez, Paz María Salazar-Schettino, Rebeca G Manning-Cela, Laila Gutiérrez-Kobeh, Guozhong Huang, Roberto Docampo
pmc-11510043.description: L-arginine metabolism through arginases and inducible nitric oxide synthase (NOS2) constitutes a fundamental axis for the resolution or progression of Chagas disease. Infection with Trypanosoma cruzi can cause a wide spectrum of disease, ranging from acute forms contained by the host immune response to chronic ones, such as the chronic chagasic cardiomyopathy.

pmc-11642364.title: Analysing Digital Engagement Patterns: A Machine Learning Investigation into Social Anxiety Among Adolescents with ADHD
pmc-11642364.creator: Roxana Șipoș, Tudor Văidean, Andreea-Marlena Răpciuc, Costina-Ruxandra Poetar, Elena Predescu, Icro Maremmani
pmc-11642364.description: Background: The relationship between screen time and mental health among adolescents, particularly those identified as “digital natives”, has become increasingly pertinent, especially in the context of heightened digital engagement during the COVID-19 pandemic. This study aims to examine the associations between digital engagement patterns, ADHD severity, and anxiety symptoms in adolescents aged 11–18.

pmc-11679515.title: Age–Stage, Two-Sex Life Table Analysis of Riptortus pedestris (Hemiptera: Alydidae) Across Different Soybean Varieties
pmc-11679515.creator: Juan Cui, Jingxu Yin, Xinyue Tian, Yu Gao, Shusen Shi, Wenbo Li
pmc-11679515.description: Simple SummaryRiptortus pedestris (Hemiptera: Alydidae) is a significant pest of soybeans. In this study, seven soybean varieties were selected to assess the adaptability of R. pedestris to different varieties, with biological parameters measured using an age–stage, two-sex life table method.

pmc-11691247.title: THE MORE, THE MERRIER? OLDER ADULTS’ LEISURE WITH OTHERS AND ASSOCIATIONS WITH WELL-BEING OVER TIME
pmc-11691247.creator: Amy Rauer, Meagan Stewart, Katherine Fiori, Christina Marini, Jeremy Kanter
pmc-11691247.description: The benefits of leisure for older adults are well-documented, as is the key role that social networks play in facilitating more opportunities for leisure. However, it is unclear if these opportunities are uniformly beneficial over time or if engaging in leisure with certain social ties (or alone) are more advantageous, particularly when barriers to social activities are greater (i.e.

pmc-12693952.title: Nutrition and Hydration at the End of Life in Intensive Care and General End-of-Life Care Settings: Balancing Clinical Evidence, Patient-Centered Care, and Ethical and Legal Principles—A Narrative Review
pmc-12693952.creator: Mircea Stoian, Adina Stoian, Claudia Bănescu, Sergio Rares Bandila, Dragoș-Florin Babă, Leonard Azamfirei, Debasis Bagchi
pmc-12693952.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Background/Objectives: Nutrition at the end of life raises many dilemmas. “End of life” refers to the period associated with a progressive incurable disease, with a life expectancy of less than six months, and limited curative treatments. In intensive care units (ICUs), decisions about artificial nutrition and hydration (clinically assisted nutrition and hydration, CANH) are especially complex because patient goals shift from survival to comfort. Nutrition and hydration are often requested by patients and their families, even when clinical benefits are uncertain.

pmc-13213463.title: Nutrition and growth of primary ciliary dyskinesia patients: a systematic review
pmc-13213463.creator: Nena Karavasiloglou, Vasiliki Gkatzou, Andrea Fernandez-Rodriguez, Valérie Schwartz, Myrofora Goutaki
pmc-13213463.description: Graphical abstract This systematic review reports on growth and nutrition-related outcomes in people with primary ciliary dyskinesia (PCD) and highlights the need for their timely and frequent assessment as standards of care. BMI: body mass index. Introduction The relationship between growth, nutrition and respiratory diseases is multifaceted and potentially bidirectional.

pmc-13247835.title: Exercise Therapy to Reduce Anxiety (ExTRA) in mid-life and later-life adults: pilot feasibility study
pmc-13247835.creator: Terence W H Chong, Andi Partovi, Julia McCurry, Eleanor Curran, David Ames, Kaarin J Anstey, Alex Bahar-Fuchs, Christina Bryant, Kay L Cox, Samantha M Loi, Jenny Southam, Alissa Westphal, Nicola T Lautenschlager
pmc-13247835.description: BackgroundAnxiety is the most prevalent mental health condition, causing significant distress, disability and cost.AimsThis pilot study assessed the feasibility and acceptability of an eight-week self-directed online exercise intervention, supported by wearable activity monitors (WAMs), for mid-life and later-life adults with clinically significant anxiety, and provided preliminary estimates of effectiveness.

pmc-13357486.title: A review on natural enzyme inhibitors: an effective approach to control postprandial hyperglycemia in type II diabetes
pmc-13357486.creator: Faezeh Shirkhan, Saeed Mirdamadi, Behrouz Akbari-adergani, Hadis Aryaee
pmc-13357486.description: Type II diabetes (T2D) is a chronic disease caused by hyperglycemia, insulin resistance, and insufficient insulin production. Inhibition of α-amylase, α-glucosidase, and dipeptidyl peptidase (DPP-IV) enzymes is considered a crucial interventional approach in managing T2D. Therefore, identification of natural enzyme inhibitors is essential.

pmc-13398502.title: Genotype by Environment Interaction for Agro‐Morphological Traits and Grain Yield Stability in Barley ( Hordeum vulgare L.) Genotypes Using AMMI Analysis Under Acidic Soil Conditions in Ethiopia

pmc-13443792.title: Brain-wide information flow dynamics during novel visual processing in humans
pmc-13443792.creator: Wushuang Huang, Jianping Song, Jingru Huangfu, Shanshan Liang, Zhiji Wang, Xiang Liao, Chunqing Zhang, Xiaowei Chen, Rongdi Yuan, Lukang Wang
pmc-13443792.description: The human brain’s capacity for visual information processing is essential for higher-order cognitive functions, including facial recognition and spatial navigation. However, the millisecond-scale dynamics of cortico-subcortical information flow during novel visual stimulation remain unclear. To investigate this, we conducted intracranial electroencephalography (iEEG) recordings in 22 patients with refractory epilepsy as they underwent a picture-viewing task.

pmc-13640342.title: Identification of potential biological biomarkers for acute ischemic stroke based on integrated bioinformatics analyses
pmc-13640342.creator: Linling Ji, Lin Zhu, Yiran Zhu, Kaiqi Ren, Jingyan Liang, Yingge Wang
pmc-13640342.description: Ischemic stroke is a major cause of disability and mortality worldwide, accounting for approximately 66% of all stroke cases. Stroke has been reported to cause approximately 6.5 million deaths annually, and the global disability-adjusted life years attributable to stroke are projected to exceed 200 million by 2030.
